{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --partition=prod
#   --job-name=XXXXXX
#   --time=12:00:00
#   --ntasks-per-node=24
#   -o XXXXXX.out

# This job appears to intend 24 MPI ranks on one node (since only ntasks-per-node is specified).
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 24
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=12h
#flux: --job-name=XXXXXX
#flux: --output=XXXXXX.out

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=prod
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-node=24 (explicit per-node placement)
# Flux does not have a universally portable batch directive for tasks-per-node.
# Performance implication: if the job were to span multiple nodes, rank placement might differ; here we force -N 1 to preserve intent.

module load openmpi
module load gromacs/5.1.4-single

# Slurm used mpirun; under Flux, use flux-run to launch MPI ranks across the allocation.
flux run -n 24 -c 1 gmx_mpi mdrun -deffnm XXXXXX
"
}
